title: Sun as a Star
questionReadAloudEn:
The Sun is a star!
Why does the sun look bigger and
brighter than the other stars?
 )

title: Earth Gravity
questionReadAloudEn: What is Earth’s gravity?
answerReadAloudEn:
An invisible force pulls all objects
toward the Earth’s center.

title: Day and Night
questionReadAloudEn:
1.​What causes day and night on
 Earth?
 2.​Which part of the Earth has
 day and which part has night?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​Day and night happen because
 the Earth spins (rotates).
 2.​ The part of Earth that is facing
 the Sun has day, and the part
 that is facing away has night.

title: Orbit and Year
questionReadAloudEn:
1.​How does the Sun’s gravity affect
 the Earth?
 2.​Why is a year 365 days long?
answerReadAloudEn:
1.​The Sun’s gravity causes the Earth
 to go around (revolve) the Sun.
 2.​It takes 365 days for Earth to go all
 the way around the Sun.

title: Sky Changes
questionReadAloudEn:
Why do we see the Sun, Moon, and
stars in different places in the sky
at different times?
answerReadAloudEn:
We see these objects in different
places in the sky because the Earth
is both spinning (rotating) and
moving around (revolving) the
Sun.

title: Seasonal Shadows
questionReadAloudEn:
Why are shadows shorter in the
summer than in the winter?
answerReadAloudEn:
In the summer, the Sun is higher in
the sky, so it makes shorter
shadows. That’s also why days are
longer in the summer.
(In the winter it is the opposite. The Sun is lower in the
sky and so the shadows are longer and the days are
shorter.)

title: Properties of Substances
questionReadAloudEn: List at least three properties we can use to describe and compare substances.
answerReadAloudEn: Properties include color, hardness, shininess, magnetism, conductivity, and solubility.

title: States of Matter
questionReadAloudEn: What are the three states of matter on Earth and how do their particles behave?
answerReadAloudEn: Solids have particles packed closely that only vibrate. Liquids have particles that move around more and are a little spread out. Gases have particles that move quickly and are very far apart.

title: Phase Change
questionReadAloudEn: What is a phase change?
answerReadAloudEn: A phase change is when matter changes from one state to another.

title: Heating and Cooling Matter
questionReadAloudEn: What happens when you add heat to a substance? What happens when you take away heat from a substance?
answerReadAloudEn: Adding heat can make solids melt into liquids and liquids evaporate into gases. Taking away heat can make gases condense into liquids and liquids freeze into solids.

title: Gases
questionReadAloudEn: What is special about gases compared to the other states of matter?
answerReadAloudEn: Gas particles always take up the amount of space available. They expand to fill a space or come closer together when compressed.

title: Conservation of Mass
questionReadAloudEn: What happens to the mass of matter when it changes form or mixes with something else?
answerReadAloudEn: The mass stays the same as long as it is in a closed system. Matter can change form, but it does not disappear.

title: Mixture vs Chemical Reaction
questionReadAloudEn: What is the difference between a mixture and a chemical reaction?
answerReadAloudEn: A mixture combines substances that can be separated back. A chemical reaction combines substances and makes a new substance that cannot be separated easily.

title: Water Cycle Steps
questionReadAloudEn: Identify the different steps of the water cycle in the picture.
answerReadAloudEn: The water cycle includes evaporation, condensation, precipitation, absorption, and runoff.

title: Saltwater and Freshwater
questionReadAloudEn: What are the major places we can find saltwater on Earth? What are the major places we can find freshwater on Earth?
answerReadAloudEn: Saltwater is found in oceans, seas, gulfs, and bays. Freshwater is found in rivers, lakes, groundwater, and glaciers or polar ice caps.

title: Drinkable Water
questionReadAloudEn: Most of Earth is covered with water, but we cannot drink most of it. What are the two reasons?
answerReadAloudEn: Most water on Earth is saltwater that we cannot drink. Most freshwater is frozen in glaciers and polar ice caps.

title: Reducing Water Pollution
questionReadAloudEn: What are three ways humans can help stop pollution of Earth’s water cycle?
answerReadAloudEn: Humans can use water treatment plants, reduce runoff from farms by creating natural filters, and reduce pollution and litter on the ground.

title: Water Filters
questionReadAloudEn: What should you think about when deciding what materials to use to make a water filter? How can you tell if a water filter is working?
answerReadAloudEn: You should consider the size of the particles you are trying to filter out. You can tell it is working if the water is clear.

title: Photosynthesis
questionReadAloudEn: How do plants make their own food and grow? What is this process called?
answerReadAloudEn: Plants use sunlight, air, and water to make sugar in their leaves. This process is called photosynthesis.

title: Organism Energy
questionReadAloudEn: Describe how producers, consumers, and decomposers get their energy.
answerReadAloudEn: Producers make their own energy through photosynthesis. Consumers get energy by eating other organisms. Decomposers get energy by breaking down dead plants and animals.

title: Matter in Ecosystems
questionReadAloudEn: Finish this chart to show how matter moves through an ecosystem.
answerReadAloudEn: Matter moves from producers to consumers to decomposers and back to soil and air.

title: Energy Starts
questionReadAloudEn: Where does energy begin in an ecosystem? Explain why.
answerReadAloudEn: Energy begins with the Sun because the Sun gives energy to producers to make their own food, which starts the cycle of energy through an ecosystem.

title: Animal Energy Uses
questionReadAloudEn: What are two examples of how animals use the energy they get from food?
answerReadAloudEn: Animals use energy from food to grow, move, stay warm, repair their bodies, and reproduce.

title: Composter
questionReadAloudEn: What is a composter? What are the four major qualities of a good composter?
answerReadAloudEn: A composter is a device created by humans to help break down food scraps into soil. A good composter lets air in, keeps the right amount of moisture, is easy to open, and keeps pests out.

title: Engineering Design Process
questionReadAloudEn: What is the engineering design process?
answerReadAloudEn: The engineering design process is the set of steps engineers follow when creating solutions to solve a problem.

title: Criteria and Constraints
questionReadAloudEn: What are criteria and constraints?
answerReadAloudEn: Criteria are the things that make it a good solution. Constraints are what you are allowed to work with.
